Publish the image where an outsider can fetch and boot it, and write the instructions that make that possible without a Thermite installation. The upstream builds this image and throws it away; this atom is the difference.

CI green on ubuntu-24.04/x86-64 (run 30779676660, 4m06s): check-fork, two
builds byte-identical, verify-build valid=true, 6/6 QEMU scenarios, artifact
uploaded. The uploaded artifact was downloaded and booted on the macOS/arm64
host following docs/running.md — 67108864 bytes, digest matches CI's, boots to
THERMITE_SUCCESS. The published artifact is runnable by someone who has never
built it.

Two script defects surfaced only in CI and are worth recording, because both
passed locally:

  - `oras` is not in Ubuntu's archives; the first run died at apt. It is only
    needed by the tag-gated publish job and now installs from its release
    tarball there.
  - `git clone` refuses a non-empty destination, and the rust-cache action
    restores .build/thermite/target before the scripts run. The first CI run
    passed only because the cache was cold; the next one failed. Both scripts
    now init-and-fetch.

The second one is the instructive one: a green first run was not evidence the
script worked, and would not have been caught by any amount of local testing
that started from a clean tree.

GHCR push remains unexecuted — tag-gated, and no tag exists.

GHCR push executed for the first time, on tag v0.1.1-alpha.1 (run 30821149593).
Both jobs green. oras reported:

  Uploaded  2ef4fdad0bef bulla.img
  Pushed [registry] ghcr.io/bulla-systems/bulla:v0.1.1-alpha.1
  ArtifactType: application/vnd.bulla.kernel-image.v1
  Digest: sha256:178487ec2ba17f66aba803eca23deb51792488bef1d395ba842d223745ce056e

The blob digest 2ef4fdad0bef matches the image digest built and booted on both
hosts, so the right bytes went up.

NOT yet verified: fetching it back. The package is private (the repository is),
and the local gh token lacks read:packages, so `oras manifest fetch` returns
`denied`. The push is evidenced by CI's own output; a round-trip pull-and-boot
is not evidenced. Those are different claims and only the first is made.

docs/running.md previously showed a bare `oras pull` with no authentication
step, which would have read as "artifact missing" to anyone without the scope.
Fixed.
